title: Finding report (a shard's return, or an aggregate over shards)
description: The one report shape in the workflow. It replaces conformance-report and inconsistency-report, which differed only in their finding vocabularies while sharing a scope object, a findings array, and a clean flag. The producing pass is named by `pass`; the finding vocabulary is the union, and each type belongs to exactly one pass. A shard returns this object and writes nothing; the orchestrator persists it.

pass.description: Which detection pass produced this report. conformance = mverify checking shipped code against the change/plan/spec that specified it. inconsistency = mreverse comparing code against code, within a repo or across a boundary.

shard.description: The conformance shard kind that produced this report. Absent on an aggregate and on an inconsistency report. Distinct from scope.kind, which is the granularity axis: `cross-repo` appears on both and means different things -- here, the shared-interface sweep; there, that the report spans repos.

repo.description: Repo under review. Omitted on cross-repo and aggregate scopes.

repos.description: The repos compared, on a cross-repo scope.

module.description: Module TAG, on a module scope.

interface.description: Shared interface TAG, on a cross-repo conformance shard.

boundary.description: The contract boundary compared, on a cross-repo inconsistency report.

change_ref.description: The change/plan/spec unit this shard was checked against.

clean.description: True iff findings is empty. On an aggregate, true iff no shard reported a finding. A clean result is a real result and is reported, never omitted.

type.description: The first six belong to the conformance pass, the last nine to the inconsistency pass. missing/extra/mismatch = change<->code surface drift; coupling = a cross-module IMPLEMENTATION import or a cross-repo reference bypassing context/shared/spec/; cross-repo-drift = a producer or consumer that does not match the frozen shared contract; stale-contract-revision = delivered code conforming to the agreement revision it was built against and to no other. That last is deliberately its own type rather than a cross-repo-drift, because the remedy differs: drift means somebody diverged and wants investigating, whereas a stale revision means the contract moved underneath conforming work and wants scheduling.

repos.description: The repos that disagree, on a cross-repo finding.

spec_ref.description: The spec or contract surface the code was checked against (file + signature/type).

code_path.description: Source path, relative to repos/<repo>/, where the finding lives.

code_refs.description: Source locations evidencing an inconsistency finding.

surface.description: The specific signature, type, endpoint or event affected.

built_against.description: On a stale-contract-revision finding: the agreement revision the delivered code was built against.

current_revision.description: On a stale-contract-revision finding: the revision the agreement now carries. With built_against this makes the gap legible without re-deriving it.
